transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Well, I'm here because of my eating habits. On these late work nights, I’ll order what I tell myself is just going to be dinner. But it always turns into a whole entrée, sides, dessert, and then I'll even get extra snacks out of my kitchen. It just ends up being way more food than I’d ever eat if someone were actually sitting across from me.
Do you find yourself eating much more quickly than normal or eating until you feel uncomfortably full during these episodes?

Yeah, definitely the speed. I eat so fast at my desk that I barely even notice the taste. I'm usually just sitting there with my Illustrator files open, and I just move from one container to the next. Then I look down and realize I’ve swallowed most of the food in just a few minutes.
Do you feel upset, embarrassed, or guilty after these eating episodes, or does it affect your work or personal life in any way?

I'm not really sure if I'd use those words. I don't really feel... guilty, I guess? Or embarrassed, mostly because I'm just by myself anyway, so there's no one around to see it. And as far as my work or personal life goes, I haven't really noticed it affecting anything. I'm already sitting there working on my designs when it happens, so it doesn't really stop me from getting my job done.
Do you usually eat large amounts of food even when you're not really hungry, or does it mostly happen when you're feeling hungry after work?

Well, a lot of the time it actually starts after I've already had a normal dinner. So, I'm not physically hungry at all, really. But I'll still find myself wandering into the kitchen, or I'll just go ahead and order delivery while I'm sitting there trying to finish a project. It doesn't seem to have much to do with whether I'm actually hungry or not.
How often do these episodes happen? Like, how many times a week or month would you say this occurs?

I'd say... well, when I look back at my delivery receipts and my calendar, there's usually at least one night every week where this happens. Sometimes it's more than that. And that pattern has been going on for several months now.
After these eating episodes, do you ever try to compensate by making yourself sick, using laxatives, or doing extra exercise?
No, I don't do any of that. I just... go to bed, usually. I don't try to throw up or take anything, and I definitely don't work out extra to make up for it. I just move on to the next day.
Do you ever feel distressed or notice any negative impact on your daily functioning because of these eating episodes?

I haven't really noticed it affecting my day-to-day life, no. I mean... I still get all my design projects done on time and everything. I'm not really sure if I'd say I feel distressed by it, either. I mostly just wake up the next morning and go about my normal routine.
During these episodes, do you feel like you can’t stop eating or control what or how much you’re eating?

Yeah, I do. It's like... once I start, there’s this point where I’m almost just watching myself keep going back to the food or opening another package. I'll be thinking that I should really stop, but it just feels like the decision has already slipped out of my hands completely.
Do you ever feel frustrated, upset, or disappointed with yourself specifically about these eating episodes, even if you don’t feel guilty or embarrassed?

No, not really. I mean, I don't feel frustrated or upset about it. Like I said, I just kind of move on. It happens, and then it's over, and I don't really dwell on it or feel disappointed in myself afterward. I just go to sleep and start the next day.

Even if you don’t feel guilty or frustrated right after, do you ever feel really upset or distressed while you're in the middle of one of these episodes, like you're losing control and can't stop yourself?

No, I wouldn't say I feel upset while it's happening, either. I definitely feel that loss of control, like I was saying, where I know I can't stop myself. But it doesn't really make me distressed in the moment. I just kind of... keep going. It's not really an emotional thing for me while I'm actually doing it.
Do you ever feel really upset, bothered, or distressed about these eating episodes overall, even if it’s not right during or right after them?

No, not really. I mean, I guess I know it's probably not the best habit, but it doesn't really bother me in the grand scheme of things. I don't sit around stressing over it or feeling upset about the fact that I do it. It's just... a thing that happens, and I don't really think much about it otherwise.
Do you ever feel any significant distress or concern about your eating behavior, even if it's not tied to guilt, embarrassment, or frustration?

No, honestly I don't. I know you've asked it a few different ways now, but I really don't have any major concern or distress about it. It's just a pattern I have, and it doesn't cause me any real worry or upset in my day-to-day life.
Do you ever feel significant distress or concern about your body shape or weight related to these eating episodes?
No, I don't. My weight and how I look... it just is what it is. I don't really stress about it or tie it back to the eating. It's just not something that bothers me.
